comparison: Perfect agreement on expression pattern data (C38-C45, C159-C161). Both evaluations find the in situ hybridization data showing spatial expression patterns to be well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes appropriate controls and multiple developmental stages; peer reviewers note 'data of the highest quality.'

Perfect agreement on SerpinE2 knockdown experiments (C2-C3, C46-C55). Both evaluations strongly support these findings. OpenEval highlights morpholino controls and rescue experiments; peer reviewers explicitly praise the 'remarkable' phenocopy of classical NC extirpations.

Perfect agreement on HtrA1 gain-of-function experiments (C4, C56-C66). Both evaluations support the concentration-dependent effects and specificity. OpenEval notes the asymmetry in knockdown effects warrants discussion; peer reviewers accept the data as 'rigorous' without raising concerns.

Strong agreement on cartilage phenotype data (C73-C82, C166). Both evaluations support the Sox9 and Alcian Blue findings with quantification. OpenEval emphasizes rescue experiments and developmental timing controls; peer reviewers accept the craniofacial defect data without question.

Perfect agreement on explant migration assays (C83-C91). Both evaluations support the NC-autonomous effects demonstrated in vitro. OpenEval highlights the isolation from surrounding tissues; peer reviewers note the 'exceptional' additional evidence.

Perfect agreement on single-cell adhesion assays (C92-C96, C203). Both evaluations support the fibronectin adhesion defects. OpenEval emphasizes quantification and controls; peer reviewers accept the data as supporting the authors' conclusions.

Perfect agreement on HtrA1 structure-function analysis (C101-C106, C175-C177). Both evaluations support the conclusion that HtrA1 acts extracellularly via protease activity. OpenEval details the mutant constructs; peer reviewers implicitly endorse through praise of 'rigorous biochemical assays.'

Perfect agreement on SerpinE2 structure-function analysis (C109-C115, C179-C181). Both evaluations support the extracellular protease inhibition mechanism via RCL. OpenEval emphasizes rescue with mutant constructs; peer reviewers accept without challenge.

Strong agreement on epistatic experiments (C5-C6, C116-C117, C134, C164). Both evaluations strongly support the double knockdown rescue demonstrating the SerpinE2-HtrA1 regulatory relationship. OpenEval calls this 'compelling evidence'; peer reviewers note it is 'remarkable.'

Strong agreement on Sdc4 rescue experiments (C9-C10, C125-C128, C189-C190). Both evaluations support the partial rescue and epistatic logic. OpenEval notes the partial nature indicates other targets exist; peer reviewers explicitly endorse the SerpinE2-HtrA1-Sdc4 pathway as 'crucial.'

Strong agreement on the integrated double-inhibition model (C11, C136-C138). Both evaluations support the pathway model. OpenEval notes appropriate caveats about additional targets; peer reviewers call the discovery 'significant' and state it 'substantially advances our understanding.'

Divergent evaluations of the gradient model (C162, C198-C199, C209-C210).
